narrative.title: Four-Way Calibration to a Target Offset
narrative.scenario: A calibration rig adjusts four independent dials recorded as signed integers and needs every distinct combination of four readings that lands exactly on a target offset. Each reading may be used at most once per combination, and combinations are reported by their values so reorderings count once.
narrative.inputFormat: An array nums of n integers and an integer target.
narrative.outputFormat: All distinct quadruples of values from nums that sum to target, with no duplicates and order not significant.
constraints: The quadruple requires four distinct indices

testCases.explanation: Three distinct value sets reach the target, with the repeated zero used at two different positions in one of them.
Only one distinct quadruple exists even though the value 2 can be chosen in many ways.

hintLevels: Level 1: Extend the pair-anchor idea one level: pin two readings and the problem collapses to finding a pair with a known complement.
Level 2: Sort, then loop over the first two anchors and converge two pointers on the suffix, recording a quadruple whenever the running pair sum matches the residual target.

Level 3: Skipping duplicates is needed at every level, not just on the middle pointers, and combining four readings near the integer limit can overflow a 32-bit sum, so widen the arithmetic before comparing.
